<strong>Apunta el dominio antes de despe: Write down the domain before isolating the unknown. Denominators that cannot be zero, radicands that cannot be negative, logarithms of positive numbers. Spurious solutions are not discovered at the end: they are avoided at the start.
<strong>Discutir es clasificar, no resol: Discussing is classifying, not solving. First the values of the parameter that make the determinant vanish, and only then is each case solved. Whoever starts by solving ends up solving three times.
<strong>En matrices, el orden importa.</: In matrices, the order matters. $AB$ and $BA$ are not the same thing and almost no exercise lets it pass. Before multiplying, check that the dimensions fit, and when isolating, multiply by the inverse on the same side of both members.
<strong>Factoriza siempre que puedas.</s: Factorise whenever you can. A factorised equation is solved by looking at it, and a factorised algebraic fraction simplifies itself. Nearly all the algebra in this block is looking for the form in which the problem is already solved.
Al resolver una ecuación con raíces obti: When solving an equation with radicals you get two solutions and only one satisfies the original equation. What has happened?
Cada tramo aporta un número fijo de preg: Each section contributes a fixed number of questions, drawn at random from its topics without repeating a topic while that is possible, and avoiding the most basic exercises. With 15 topics and 10 questions, a single exam does not touch them all: that is why the link at the end reproduces the same exam, and “another exam” draws a different one.
Cómo sacarle partido: How to get the most out of it
El enlace de un examen corregido reprodu: The link to a marked exam reproduces the same questions with the same numbers. A teacher can do one, copy the link and pass it to the class: everyone will sit the same exam and will be able to compare results and procedures.
Elevar al cuadrado ha añadido una soluci: Squaring has added a solution that was not there
Elevar al cuadrado no es reversible: de: Squaring is not reversible: from $a = b$ you go to $a^2 = b^2$, which $a = -b$ also satisfies. That is why every equation with radicals ends by checking the solutions in the original one.
Elige los tramos que entran. Las pregunt: Choose the sections to include. The questions are drawn at random from the exercises of each topic in the block, avoiding the most basic ones and without repeating a topic while possible. There are no hints: the marking and the step-by-step solution come on submitting.
Hay un error de cuenta en algún paso: There is an arithmetic slip somewhere
La ecuación tiene dos soluciones y una s: The equation has two solutions and one falls outside the domain of the reals
La palabra «álgebra» viene del título de: The word “algebra” comes from the title of the book al-Khwarizmi wrote in Baghdad around the year 820: al-jabr, “the restoring”, the step of taking negative terms to the other side. That book had no symbols: the problems and the solutions were written out in words, and each kind of equation was a separate case with its own recipe. Putting a letter where a whole sentence used to be is what turned fourteen recipes into a single method, and it is what is asked about here.
Multiplicar matrices y cuidar el orden;: Multiplying matrices and minding the order; computing a determinant of order 3; finding the rank by minors; inverting a matrix and isolating the unknown in a matrix equation; complex numbers in rectangular and polar form.
No es cuestión de reales: las dos son nú: It is not a question of reals: both are perfectly ordinary real numbers. What fails is that one does not satisfy the starting equation, only the squared one.
Operar con monomios y sacar factor común: Operating with monomials and taking out a common factor; dividing by synthetic division and using the remainder theorem; factorising with the standard identities; simplifying an algebraic fraction and saying which values the denominator forbids.
Puede haberlo, pero la solución de más a: There may be one, but the extra solution appears even with perfect arithmetic: the method itself introduces it. Checking in the original equation is not optional.
Quince temas que van de poner una letra: Fifteen topics that go from putting a letter where a number was to discussing a system with a parameter, which is the last thing the entrance exam asks. This topic teaches nothing new: it asks. A procedural exam with exercises from the whole block, with a clock and no hints, to know whether the algebra now comes without thinking about every step.
Resolver de primer y de segundo grado y: Solving linear and quadratic equations and reading the discriminant; systems by substitution or equating; inequalities with the sign line; exponential and logarithmic equations while checking the domain.
Triangular por Gauss y leer la solución;: Triangularising by Gaussian elimination and reading off the solution; classifying by the Rouché-Frobenius theorem; discussing according to a parameter, saying for which values the system has a unique solution, infinitely many, or none.
Un examen de bloque es un simulacro hech: A block exam is a mock paper taken at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. The questions come from the exercises of the 15 topics of the block, spread across sections, and every time you start one the numbers are different and so are the topics: doing it several times covers the whole block. On submission everything is marked, the step-by-step solution of each question opens, and the mark comes out section by section, with links to what is worth revising. The “tailored to what you have done” option puts first what you have not solved yet: it is the way to check that no topic is left untouched.
